meta.title: Valheim guide: what the game never tells you — Seed Archive
meta.description: From the first beehive in the Meadows to Kall in the Deep North: what each land asks of you, what it gives, and the odds the game never shows.

home.title: What the game never tells you
home.lead: A Valkyrie drops you by the stones of the tenth world, Hugin the raven gives you his first tip, and Odin gives you a task: put down his enemies, one in each land. Eight lands lie ahead, from the soft <meadows>Meadows</meadows> to the <deepNorth>Deep North</deepNorth>. Valheim never tells you the odds. We do, from your <basics>first steps</basics> to the end. Want it harder? Take on the <challenges>challenges</challenges>. Whichever road you take, every weapon, meal and boss you meet on it waits in the <catalog>catalog</catalog>. And before you set sail, drop your <map>seed on the map</map> and find out if it is <rating>good enough</rating> to grow into Yggdrasil.

meadows.name: Meadows
meadows.hook: Where every game begins: Eikthyr, the hives in the houses you rob, the first pickaxe.

black-forest.name: Black Forest
black-forest.hook: Copper, tin and the Elder, and the trolls that guard all three.

swamp.name: Swamp
swamp.hook: Iron sleeps in the Sunken Crypts, and so do the bones that wake Bonemass.

mountain.name: Mountain
mountain.hook: Silver under the snow, wolves on the slopes, Moder's eggs on the peaks.

plains.name: Plains
plains.hook: Black metal, Fuling villages and the totems Yagluth asks for.

mistlands.name: Mistlands
mistlands.hook: Black cores in the mist, and the Queen beneath it.

ashlands.name: Ashlands
ashlands.hook: A sea that burns your boat, fortresses of the Charred, and Fader.

deep-north.name: Deep North
deep-north.hook: The newest land: Kall waits at its end and calls back every boss before him.

meta.title: Forge of Potential without breaking: pick a name in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Pick an idol, an item and a step at the Forge of Potential, and get the character names whose first try raises it instead of breaking it.

forgeName.title: Nidavellir
forgeName.subtitle: In Norse myth, Nidavellir is the home of the dwarves, where the brothers Sindri and Brokkr forged Thor's hammer Mjölnir. Here it is the place to find the name that forges your item without breaking it.
forgeName.question: How do I raise an item at the Forge of Potential without breaking it?
forgeName.again: A name is no luck charm: for a second copy of the same item, every level is its second try, and can break where the first copy rose. Each copy needs fresh characters of its own.
forgeName.answer: Give the character who presses the button the right name. The forge's first try of an item at a level is decided by the character's name alone, so pick the idol, the item and the step, and take a name whose first try raises it.
forgeName.guide: What goes to the forge, what a try takes and why a name decides it are in the guide <link>Forge of Potential</link>.
forgeName.names: Names whose first try raises it to level {to}:

how.title: How to raise an item with a name
how.lead: One step, one fresh character with a name from above, written exactly. It takes the item, its idol, the recipe's ingredients and warm clothes from a chest at your base, walks past the station that makes the item, and presses the forge's button once. A name holds for the first try of each item at each level; delete the character and make it again, and its tries start over.
how.why: Why the ingredients: the forge lists only the recipes a character knows, and a fresh one learns a recipe by holding all its ingredients and standing by its station.
how.steps: Every step, from the stations to the name, is in the guide's section <steps>How do I raise an item without breaking it?</steps>, and the ingredients each item's recipe asks for, the ones that go in the chest, are in the <catalog>Catalog</catalog>.

howToRead.title: How to read the report
howToRead.where: Every distance in a question comes from a scan of many seeds: it is how far three seeds in four have what the run needs, rounded to ten metres. The count before it is what the run asks for: the eggs for Moder, the totems for Yagluth, the cores for a smelter, a kiln and a pair of portals.
howToRead.colour: The colour of an answer is where your seed stands among the scanned ones. Green: the best quarter, the thing lies nearer than on three seeds in four. Grey: the usual middle half. Red: the worst quarter, or none within the distance at all. A count with no need, such as the oaks or the black cores, is coloured the same way by its own quarters. A boss or trader in the strip is green, outside it red. A row left grey is the same on almost every seed and does not count.
howToRead.score: Each green answer gives a block one point, each grey one half, each red none; a block's number is the share it gets of all its answers, and the seed's number the mean of its blocks.

meta.title: Bugs: why one seed gives different crypts in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Why Burial Chambers and Sunken Crypts differ on one seed, why the map's loot is an average, and why the Helmet of the Protector never reaches the forge.

bugs.title: Bugs
bugs.lead: Why does a Burial Chamber on my seed have other rooms than on a friend's, on the very same seed? Because the game turns each Burial Chamber and Sunken Crypt at random, apart from the seed, and the turn decides its rooms.

crypts.title: Burial Chambers and Sunken Crypts differ on the same seed
crypts.how: The game sets every location down at one of {yaws, plural, one {# turn} other {# turns}}, {step}° apart, and picks the turn with a random number that the seed does not fix. For most locations the turn changes nothing inside. A Burial Chamber in the Black Forest and a Sunken Crypt in the Swamp are different: the turn shifts the dungeon's generator a little, and the generator's position becomes the seed of the dungeon's rooms.
crypts.cores: So one crypt on one seed has a few possible layouts, each with its own rooms, chests, surtling cores and scrap piles. Which one a world gets is settled when the crypt is first generated, and stays.
crypts.others: Troll caves, frost caves, Infested Mines and the other dungeons are not touched by it: their rooms follow from the seed alone.
crypts.maps: A seed map that shows a single layout for a crypt shows one of its possible layouts. What a world really holds is in its save, once someone has walked in.

loot.title: Why the map's loot is an average
loot.why: Click a dungeon or a camp on the map and its panel lists what it holds. Some numbers there are exact, others are averages, for two reasons: the turn of the crypts above, and chests that roll their contents only when opened. The panel sorts every line into one of three groups.
loot.exact: Stands there. Fixed by the seed: the same in every world made from it, so the number is exact.
loot.overYaws: Stands there, by its turn. What stands in a Burial Chamber or a Sunken Crypt: its rooms' cores and scrap piles. The crypt is built one of {yaws, plural, one {# way} other {# ways}}, so the panel gives the average of them, with the fewest and the most a crypt of that place can have. Your world holds one of those layouts.
loot.atPlay: Rolled when you take it. Chests, and what drops from things you break, are rolled by the game when you open or break them, not when the world is made. No map can know them; the panel gives the average the game's own odds give.

protector.title: The Helmet of the Protector never reaches the Forge of Potential
protector.why: The Forge of Potential lists an item only when its recipe asks for an idol. Every other weapon and piece of armour that rises past its last level asks for one; the Helmet of the Protector does not: its recipe holds gold, its mould and moose hide, and nothing else.
protector.what: So the forge never offers it, and the helmet stays at level {max}, while the chest and legs of the same set rise further. Nothing you carry changes it: the forge reads the recipe, not your inventory.

meta.description: Every raid on your base: what starts it, what ends it for good, how long it lasts, and which creatures come and how many at once.

events.title: Raids
events.question: What raids my base, and when does it stop?
events.answer: {minutes, plural, one {Every minute} other {Every # minutes}}, while you are near a base, the game rolls a {chance}% chance of a raid from those your world has opened. A raid tied to the bosses comes only between one boss and the next, so killing the next one ends it for good.
events.how: Every other raid stays once opened. And you outlast a raid rather than clear it: each kind of creature keeps coming back up to the most it can have at once, a fresh one for each you kill, until the raid's time runs out.

invasion.title: The Jotun Invasion
invasion.text: This one is no raid on your base but an event of the world, and you start it yourself: break the Malicious Ice in the halls of a Mörkhalla in the Deep North and the Jotuns advance. Up to three invasion sites stand at once, each a frozen patch of the Meadows, the Black Forest, the Swamp, the Mountain or the Plains, far from the world's centre and marked on your map; with no map, a trail of particles leads you to the nearest. Each holds until you break the Malicious Ice or the Orb of Fimbulvinter at its heart and the Jotuns retreat. Their own raid, the Jotuns at your base, begins once you have killed a Jotun and ends only with Kall Fimbulbringer.

wind.title: Wind
wind.question: Which way does the wind blow?
wind.answer: The world's clock decides it, not the seed: at the same hour of the same day the wind blows the same way in every world, so this table is your wind too.
wind.read: Each cell is where the wind comes from at the start of that game hour. The main direction holds for about {hold, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}, with smaller turns every couple of minutes on top of it. The night's hours are grey: sleep through them and you never sail in them. The first hours of day 1 are empty, since a new world begins just before its first morning.
wind.dead: The sail is dead when the wind comes from within {deg}° of the bow, on either side, {share}% of all headings, and only the oars move you then. Moder's power turns the wind dead astern while it lasts: call it when the wind stands ahead of your beam. Her power is on <link>How to kill each boss</link>.

comfort.title: Comfort
comfort.question: How do I raise comfort?
comfort.lead: Rest under a roof by one piece of each kind: a fire, a bed, a chair, a table, a banner and the rest. Only the best piece of each kind counts, so a throne beside a chair adds only the throne.

rule.title: How comfort counts
rule.rested: Rested lasts {base, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} at comfort 1, and {per, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} more for each level above it.
rule.sum: Comfort starts at {base}; a roof over you adds {shelter}. Then every piece within ten metres adds its comfort.
rule.groups: Pieces come in kinds: fires, beds, chairs, tables, banners, carpets, displays, decor, garlands, lanterns and leisure. Of each kind only the piece with the most comfort counts. A piece of no kind counts once, however many stand.
rule.lit: A fire counts only while it burns. An item stand is a display: it gives its comfort empty, and a trophy hung on it adds nothing.

byBiome.title: Comfort by biome
byBiome.text: How far your base's comfort climbs with what you can build by each biome: the best piece of each kind so far, plus every piece of no kind. Build all of it and comfort reaches {most}, and Rested lasts {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.

meta.title: All bosses and how to kill each in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Two ways to beat every boss: the hardest-hitting weapon you can make by then, and the other way players win. With health, weaknesses and attacks.

bosses.title: How to kill each boss
bosses.question: How do I kill each boss?
bosses.lead: Two ways for each, never only one: the weapon that hurts it most of what you can make by then, and the way players win without a straight fight, with fire where the boss burns. Under each, its health, its weaknesses, how long a campfire takes to burn it down and what its attacks deal; Kall phase by phase.

fire.time: a campfire alone burns it down in about {minutes} min, if it stays in the flames
fire.never: a campfire never kills it: it heals faster than the fire burns, or takes no fire

bosses.aspects: He takes no damage from you in this phase. He brings back {count, plural, one {the # earlier boss} other {the # earlier bosses}} as aspects, at most {atOnce} at a time, Eikthyr's first; each aspect's death strikes him for {blast}, so all must die. An aspect's health is its own (that of {health}), but each takes damage just as its boss does, and blunt is never weaker than full on any of them: what hurts each is in <link>the table at the top</link>.
bosses.breaks: They fell trees and break rock

direct.title: The straight fight
direct.text: What you can make by {biome} that hits it hardest, one hit counted after its weaknesses and resistances; a bow with the best arrow of the time, a crossbow with the best bolt:

power.title: The power of the trophy
power.how: Hang the trophy on its stone at the Sacrificial Stones: once you call the power it lasts {minutes} min, and you can call it again after {cooldown} min.
power.sail: The wind follows the world's clock, not your course: it holds a main direction for about {windHoldMin} min and is as likely behind you as ahead. A sail dies when the wind comes from within {sailDeadDeg}° of the bow on either side, {sailDeadShare}% of all headings, and then you row. Her power turns the wind dead astern whatever your heading, so call it when the wind stands ahead of your beam; with the wind already behind or abeam it gains you nothing.
power.sailMore: Where the wind comes from, hour by hour all year, is in the tool <link>Wind</link>.
power.none: The game gives no power for this trophy.

tip.Dragon: She fights in the air and lands only now and then, so bring a bow. The table ranks poison arrows first because it counts a hit's whole damage, but poison trickles in over a few seconds; fire, which she is weak to, lands at once, so fire arrows serve as well.

other.title: The other way
other.Eikthyr: Circle the big rocks round his altar and shoot from behind them: the rocks stop his charge, though not his stomp.
other.gd_king: Ring his platform and the gaps between the pillars with campfires: fire hurts him double, and he burns as he walks over them while you shoot from behind a pillar. Or dig under the altar: its platform is a roof he cannot break, room for a workbench and a portal.
other.Bonemass: Shoot him from above, from a stone tower or a high tree, with frost arrows; level the ground round the altar with a hoe first, so you can move and leeches keep away.
other.Dragon: Dig a trench against the side of her summoning platform, which cannot be broken, and stay in it: when she lands, her breath and claws do not reach you, and you shoot straight up. Bring a lot of arrows.
other.GoblinKing: Speedrunners circle him: stay close, keep running round to his back from the first blow to the last, and he turns too slowly to hit you. If you would rather shoot, keep a stone pillar between you and him and step out to fire: breaking his line of sight stops his beam.
other.SeekerQueen: The vestibule at her entrance is safe: she does not attack you there and nothing spawns there, so build your rest and repairs just outside.
other.Fader: Summon two trolls with the Trollstav and stay out of his reach: he fights them and leaves you alone while you do not hit him. Or dig two pits side by side and leave the ground between them as the wall, never a built one: he breaks pieces, not earth, and when he cannot reach you it is a piece he goes for. Line his pit with Ashwood stakewalls: they hurt him, but each wears out after a few hits and breaks when he walks into it, so keep repairing them from your side. Nothing can be dug by his altar: lead him out of his arena to the pits first.
other.FrozenKing: Fight each phase with what it is open to. The first and the third take half from pierce, fire, frost and lightning, so bows, spears and staffs do half: bring the heaviest blunt or slash weapon you have, and expect no stagger and no opening in either. In the second, leave him be and kill the aspects as they come: blunt hurts every one in full, the Elder's and Moder's burn, and Bonemass's and Yagluth's shrug off pierce.

traders.title: What to buy from the traders
traders.question: What to buy from the traders?
traders.answer: Haldor's Megingjord and his extra inventory rows carry more of every haul; the Bog Witch's serving tray and spices turn your cooking into feasts; Hildir sells clothes and hats, more of them with every chest you bring her back.

about.Haldor: He trades in the Black Forest: gear and the extra inventory rows, with more on his shelf as the bosses fall.
about.BogWitch: She trades in the Swamp, in what your cooking and potions need: the serving tray for feasts, each biome's spice and the ingredients of meads.
about.Hildir: She trades in the Meadows, in clothes and hats, and puts out more each time you bring back one of her chests.

sell.title: What the traders buy
sell.text: These are all a trader will buy, each for a fixed number of coins. A few also go into recipes, so think before you sell them; the rest are good for nothing but coins, and coins are good for nothing but the goods above.

quest.title: Hildir's quest
quest.text: Hildir is the only trader with a quest. Three of her chests were stolen, and each now lies in a dungeon of its own: kill its guard and the chest drops. Every chest you bring her back puts more of her goods on sale.

traders.writhan: One of her goods waits on a kill instead of a chest: the Crown of Roots goes on sale only after you kill a Writhan, a rare creature of the Swamp and no boss.

weapons.question: Which weapon to use?
weapons.lead: A sword when you attack, a mace when you hold your ground, and the mace again on the hardest settings, where it is the favourite; an atgeir against crowds, a knife from the shadows, fists if they are your style. Every one by biome, with its damage, station and materials.

meta.title: Damage types: what hurts each creature in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Every creature's and boss's weaknesses and resistances to each damage type, the weapon kind to bring, and the damage it deals back.

damage.title: Damage types
damage.question: What hurts each creature?
damage.lead: Every creature and boss by biome: the damage types it takes harder or softer, so you know which weapon kind to bring, and the damage it deals back, so you know which resistance to wear.

hurts.title: What hurts each creature
hurts.lead: A weak spot multiplies the hit, a resistance divides it. Each weapon kind deals mostly one type:
hurts.fire: Fire is the weakness you meet most often: in the Black Forest and the Mountain most creatures take it harder, which is why speedrunners burn them with campfires. Drop the habit at the Mistlands: there and in the Ashlands no creature is weak to fire, and in the Ashlands most resist it.

deals.title: What each creature hits with
deals.lead: The strongest blow of each damage type a creature can deal, before your armour: wear the resistance to its type.
deals.pierce: Pierce is what the bosses hit you with, all but Bonemass and Yagluth, and the Deathsquito of the Plains stings with nothing else. The Root Harnesk is the one chest piece that halves pierce, so wear it against them; it takes fire harder, though, so leave it at home for Yagluth. Every armour piece is on <link>Armour</link>.

meta.title: Bows, crossbows and arrows: which to pick in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: The arrow, not the bow, sets the damage type. Every bow, crossbow, arrow, bolt and bomb by biome, with its damage, station and materials.

bows.title: Bows, crossbows and arrows
bows.question: Which bow and which arrows?
bows.lead: The arrow, not the bow, sets the damage type: a bow's damage adds to its arrow's, so fire arrows for what burns, frost for what freezes. Every bow, crossbow, arrow, bolt and bomb by biome.

meta.title: Staffs: what each one casts and costs in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Every staff of elemental and blood magic by biome: what it casts or summons, what a cast costs in eitr and health, and its materials.

staffs.title: Staffs
staffs.question: What does each staff cast?
staffs.lead: Elemental staffs deal the damage themselves and cost only eitr: a fireball that bursts where it lands, a stream of frost, a volley of lightning, roots that rise and strike. Blood magic staffs put something between you and the enemy, and take a share of your health with the eitr: they raise skeletons, a troll or animal spirits, or lay a shield on you and your allies; the Echo Spike alone strikes for itself and asks no health. A summoning staff is the one worth upgrading first, since every level of it lets one more summon stand. Every staff by biome, with what a cast does and costs.
staffs.eitr: You have no eitr at all until you eat for it, and a staff without eitr casts nothing: the dishes that give it are on <link>Food and feasts</link>.

armour.question: Which armour to wear?
armour.lead: Every helmet, chest piece, leg piece, cape, shield and trinket by biome, with its armour, block and effects. Mind the speed as well as the armour: some pieces slow you more than usual for their kind, and a few make you faster.

stars.title: Stars
stars.text: A star means more health, harder hits and more drops. Each star is a roll, mostly at {chance}% (nests and a few spawners differ), rolled again for the second; a few creatures roll only far from the world's centre, and a night spawn may allow more stars than the day's. A raid's creatures come without stars, except the Ticks and the escorts of Hildir's guards. Your world's settings and some biome patches change the chance.

head.share: Of those that can have two

stars.note: Drops: both the chance and the amount of each drop.

fish.title: Fishing
fish.text: Haldor sells the rod and plain bait; every other bait is plain bait and a trophy, so the creatures you hunt decide which fish you can catch. Every fish goes into raw fish, and that is what the dishes take.
fish.where: {biomes}, in water {water} m deep or more

notes.Troll: A troll cave often holds a troll inside and sometimes one more by its entrance; neither comes back once killed. One troll in {weaponSets} carries a log: it reaches farther but never throws, while an unarmed troll punches, slams and hurls rocks from afar; otherwise they are the same troll, with the same health and drops. Kill a troll and the Elder, and trolls can raid your base. Pierce hurts them most, so bring a spear or arrows. They break walls, so no trap holds one, but lure one past trees and copper and it fells and mines for you.
notes.Bjorn: Wall a bear in on flat ground with a campfire under it and it burns; keep repairing the fire and the walls while it does.
notes.GoblinBruteBros: When Thungr falls, Zil rises from him and fights on; Zil carries Hildir's Bronze Chest.
notes.GoblinShaman_Hildir: No spawner makes him: he rises when Thungr falls, in Hildir's Sealed Tower.
notes.Serpent: A sea monster: it hunts ships in the deep ocean.
notes.BonemawSerpent: A sea monster: it hunts ships in the waters of the Ashlands.

meta.title: Farming: every crop, where it grows, how long in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: Every crop, tree and vine the cultivator plants: what it is planted with, what it gives, how long it grows, where it grows and which dishes it feeds.

farming.title: Farming
farming.question: How do I farm?
farming.lead: Every crop, tree and vine the cultivator plants: what it is planted with, what it gives, how long it grows and where it grows.
farming.cultivator: The cultivator turns ground into a field and plants seeds in it. A crop grows only on cultivated ground and only in the biomes listed beside it; a seed from one biome often grows in others, but not always where it was found.

crops.title: Crops
crops.text: A crop is planted with its seed and gives its harvest. Where the seeds do not come back with it, plant one of the harvest (or a seed, for kale) and it grows into seeds: one find keeps a field going. What each harvest goes into is on its row in <link>Materials</link>.
crops.conclusion: {biome} grow {count} of the {all, plural, one {# crop} other {# crops}}, every one but {missing}: the one farm that feeds a whole game. Some grow in one biome only, {only}: no home elsewhere grows them, so they are farmed where they grow. Your home in the Meadows grows {home} of them.
crops.sameTime: Every crop takes the same {min}–{max, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}, so a field is chosen by where it grows, not by how fast.

trees.title: Trees
trees.text: A sapling grows on any ground; what a grown tree gives when felled is its average.
trees.conclusion: The {most} is the slow one, {min}–{max, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}, and pays for it with {fine} fine wood, more than any other tree: plant oaks where you will stay. For wood you burn and build with in bulk, the {quick} is back within {quickMax, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.

vines.title: Vines
vines.text: Vines grow fastest of all and give vineberries.
vines.conclusion: A vine is ripe in {min}–{max, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}, a crop in {crop} at the least: a few vines by the door keep the vineberries coming while a field is still green.

where.title: Where should I farm?
where.text: In {biome}, once you can hold ground there: one farm grows nearly everything the game plants, so it is the field you keep to the end. Until then farm at home, where {home} of the {all, plural, one {# crop} other {# crops}} grow. What each crop then feeds is on <link>Food and feasts</link>.

meta.title: Best food for melee, archer and mage in Valheim — Seed Archive
meta.description: The best dishes for a melee fighter, an archer and a mage, biome by biome, and every dish and feast with its health, stamina and eitr.

food.title: Food and feasts
food.question: What to eat?
food.answer: Health dishes for a melee fighter, stamina dishes for an archer, eitr dishes for a mage; a feast fills one slot with all three.
food.basics: You eat up to three different dishes at once; each raises health, stamina or eitr and regenerates health while it lasts.

who.title: Who eats what
who.matrix: The three best dishes of each kind you can make by the end of each biome: eat all three, since different dishes always stack. A dish in bold is new in that biome; the others are still the best of an earlier one.
who.again: When to eat again: a dish can be eaten again once half its time has passed, and it still gives about four fifths of its value then. Eat each again at its half and the three slots stay nearly full.
who.notYet: No dish of this kind before the biome where the row starts: eitr food begins in the Mistlands, with magic.
who.feast: Feasts: health and stamina, and eitr from the Mistlands on, in one slot and for the longest time.

feasts.title: Feasts
feasts.text: Make a feast at the food preparation table and set it down on a serving tray, and the whole group eats from it.
feasts.tray: Buy the serving tray from the Bog Witch.
